close_reason: Resolved together with JMAP-826m.50. The justification string is now hoisted into the INFALLIBLE_SERIALIZE_JUSTIFICATION const at helpers.rs, so the four call sites in this crate (set_error_value, metadata_value, plus the memory.rs filter-roundtrip site that has a different argument shape and keeps its own string) reference the const or use a typed helper rather than re-inlining the literal. The 'panic-message vs reader-justification' distinction the bead noted is preserved by keeping rustdoc on each call site documenting WHY the expect is unreachable; the const itself carries only the short greppable string the user would see at runtime.
description:
What is awkward: helpers.rs:108 (and metadata.rs:373, 433) all carry the .expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible") justification string. The justification is correct, but the same string appears 3 times.

Two-part awkwardness:
(a) The justification is for the reader, but the panic-message string is what the user sees if the impossible happens. They are not the same audience. The message reads like a Rust note to the reader, not an actionable diagnostic.
(b) Could be a const fn or a helper to avoid the repeated 'plain data is infallible' string literal.

Suggested rewrite: hoist into a single helper like serialize_or_panic(&v) -> Value with the one-line justification on the helper. Both arguments (cleaner sites, single justification) move toward each other.

Filing as P3 elegance. Could mark opinion in Section 7.
title: set_error_value helper uses .expect('derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible') instead of .unwrap_or_else default value — string of justification is verbose for what should be unreachable
